issues.failure_explanation: In \autoref{eq:deeponet} the inner sum over l multiplies w_{j,k,l} by the single value x(s_j); the sensor point is indexed by j both here, in \autoref{eq:D}, and in the coefficient count N_j(...+m+...) of Theorem th:operatorapx. As written each branch term depends on one point value only, so F_n[x](t)=sum_j g_j(x(s_j))h_j(t) is additive in point values and cannot approximate e.g. F[x]=(∫x)^2, contradicting th:operatorapx. Theorems th:functional apx and th:operatorapx and \autoref{eq:nldeep} instead use x(s_l) with N_l sensors, and the parameter count in th:functional apx (N_j(N_k+2), with no N_j in the network) is also inconsistent with its own coefficient tuple.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace x(s_j) by x(s_l) in \autoref{eq:deeponet}, index s_l (l=1..N_l) in \autoref{eq:D} and th:operatorapx, and correct the counts to N_j(N_k(N_l+2)+n+1)+N_l m and N_k(N_l+2) respectively.
issues.overall_effect: The defining object of the paper is ambiguous/degenerate as written; the coefficient counts n used to parametrize approximation rates are inconsistent with the stated architecture.
issues.title: Neural operator definition indexes sensor points by j, giving a degenerate architecture inconsistent with the approximation theorems and parameter counts
issues.why_classification: Purely a local correction of indices and counts; all substantive results survive once the standard architecture is restored.

issues.failure_explanation: By \autoref{eq:expansion}, F_N^# = F Q_N with Q_N the orthogonal projector onto X_N, so Fx - F_N^# x = F(I-Q_N)x and ||Fx-F_N^# x|| ≤ ||F(I-Q_N)|| ||x||. The corollary instead bounds it by ||(I-P_N)F|| (P_N projector onto Y_N = F(X_N)), which is a different, in general smaller quantity: since F Q_N x ∈ Y_N one has (I-P_N)F = (I-P_N)F(I-Q_N), so ||(I-P_N)F|| ≤ ||F(I-Q_N)|| and not conversely. Counterexample in R^2: X_N=span{e_1}, F e_1=e_1, F e_2=e_1+εe_2 (injective); then ||(I-P_N)F||=ε but ||Fx-F_N^# x||=||e_1+εe_2||≈1 for x=e_2. Also the factor ||x|| is dropped, and ν_N→0 requires the training images to span a dense subspace (Q_N→I strongly), not compactness of F alone.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ν_N by ||F(I-Q_N)|| sup_{x∈B_ρ(x†)}||x||, and add the hypothesis that ∪X_N is dense in X (then ||F(I-Q_N)||→0 for compact F); propagate the new quantity to th:linear.
issues.overall_effect: The stated bound \autoref{eq:estimate}, the definition of ν_N and the last equality in the rate of Theorem th:linear (in terms of ν_N) are unsupported; the paper's discussion of the 'importance of ν_N' refers to the wrong quantity.
issues.title: First term of the error estimate in Corollary cor:rate is bounded by the wrong operator norm
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is false as stated and the quantity governing the rate must be replaced and an extra hypothesis added, but a comparable estimate is recovered with a short, contained argument.

issues.failure_explanation: F_N^# x - F̃_n[x] = Σ_ℓ (a_ℓ b_ℓ - ã_ℓ b̃_ℓ) with a_ℓ=<x,x̲^{(ℓ)}>, b_ℓ=y̲^{(ℓ)}, and a_ℓ b_ℓ-ã_ℓ b̃_ℓ=(a_ℓ-ã_ℓ)b_ℓ+ã_ℓ(b_ℓ-b̃_ℓ). Under \autoref{eq:qn}-\autoref{eq:rn} this gives ||F_N^# x-F̃_n[x]|| ≤ Σ_ℓ (q(N)||y̲^{(ℓ)}|| + (|a_ℓ|+q(N)) r(N)) = O(N(q(N)+r(N))), not N q(N) r(N). The product form is only obtained if one erroneously assumes both factors are simultaneously in error. Consequently the example rates N q r = 1/(N√N_j) and O(N^{-1-p/2}) are unfounded; the correct bound is O(N^{-1}+N^{1-p/2}), which is much worse and does not even decay for p≤2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace N q(N) r(N) by C N (q(N)+r(N)) in \autoref{eq:estimate} and th:linear and recompute the example rates accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The second term of \autoref{eq:estimate}, the rate expressions in the following example (\autoref{eq:estNqr} and O(N^{-1-p/2})), the remark deeming this term 'of less importance', and the final expression of the rate in Theorem th:linear are incorrect.
issues.title: Second term of \autoref{eq:estimate}: error of approximating a sum of products is bounded by a product N q(N) r(N) instead of a sum
issues.why_classification: Straightforward algebraic correction, but it materially worsens the advertised approximation term and invalidates the concrete rates given in the example; the structural conclusion survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let us assume that $\x$ and $\ulx^{(\ell)}$ are bounded between $(0,1)$.
In other words, we get an explicit formula for the coefficients, which can be chosen even independent of $N_l$.

issues.failure_explanation: The coefficients (w_k,θ_k) solving \autoref{eq:expl2} depend on the value x(t_k) of the particular input x, since a fixed sigmoid t↦σ(w t+θ) cannot equal the linear map t↦t·x̲(t_k) for all t. Hence no fixed network Σ_k C_k σ(w_k x(t_k)+θ_k) realizes the trapezoidal sum for all x in a neighborhood, and the claimed rate q(N)=N^{-2} (uniform in x, as required by \autoref{eq:qn}) is not established. Moreover the auxiliary assumption 0<x̲^{(ℓ)}<1 on (0,1) is incompatible with orthonormality in L^2(0,1) (it forces ||x̲^{(ℓ)}||^2=∫(x̲^{(ℓ)})^2<1), and products x(t_k)x̲^{(ℓ)}(t_k) need not lie in the range (0,1) of σ, so σ^{-1} is not defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the explicit formula and instead invoke a genuine neural approximation of the linear functional x↦Σ_k C_k x(t_k) (e.g. via approximating the identity by sigmoids on a bounded range) with an honest, x-independent error bound; recompute q(N).
issues.overall_effect: The 'explicit formula' for functional-approximation coefficients, the rate q(N)=N^{-2}, and the derived example rates feeding the discussion after cor:rate and the remark after th:linear are unsupported.
issues.title: Explicit construction of branch-net coefficients via σ^{-1}(x(t_k)x̲(t_k)) is input-dependent and rests on an impossible assumption
issues.why_classification: A concrete construction and its rate are lost and must be replaced by a new argument, but the surrounding theory (cor:rate, th:linear in terms of abstract q,r) is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follow easily from the Rellich-Kondrachov theorem (see \cite[Theorem 6.2]{Ada75}), which states that the embedding $H^s(\Omega_\X) \hookrightarrow C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$ is compact for $s > \frac{m}{2}$
We say that $\U$ is compact in $\V$ if every sequence in $\U$ has a subsequence that converges in the $\norms{\cdot}_V$-norm to an element in $\V$.

issues.failure_explanation: Chen–Chen's Theorems 4/5 require the functional/operator to be continuous with respect to the C(Ω̄)-topology on a C-compact set; the neural functional Σ_k C_k σ(Σ_l w_{k,l}x(s_l)+θ_k) is continuous in the sup norm. The paper replaces this by H^s-continuity, which is strictly weaker on C-compact sets. Counterexample (m=1, s=1): D(F)= closed unit ball of H^1(0,1), which is compact in C[0,1] in the sense of def:compact by Rellich–Kondrachov; F[x]=||x'||_{L^2} is H^1-continuous. For x_n=(c/n)sin(2πns) with small c, x_n→0 uniformly so F_n[x_n]→F_n[0], but F[x_n]→c√2π≠F[0]=0, so no uniform approximation with ε<c√2π/2 exists. The same F (times a constant function in L^2(Ω_Y)) refutes th:operatorapx. Rellich–Kondrachov gives C-precompactness of H^s-bounded sets but does not transfer H^s-continuity to C-continuity, so the claimed 'easy' proof is invalid.

failure_location.quote: be a continuous functional with respect to the $(H^s(\Omega_\X),\norms{\cdot}_{H^s})$-topology, and suppose that the domain $\dom{F}$ is compact in $C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require F to be continuous with respect to the C(Ω̄_X)-norm on D(F) (or require D(F) to be compact in H^s, whence the two topologies coincide on it), and note that the results then follow directly from \cite{TiaHon95}.
issues.overall_effect: Theorems th:functional apx and th:operatorapx are false as stated; the advertised extension of the universal approximation theorems 'from sets of continuous functions to Sobolev spaces' is not established. (th:l2 operator apx applies them to an L^2-continuous, hence C-continuous, F and is not affected by this root.)
issues.title: Sobolev versions of the universal approximation theorems are false: H^s-continuity on a C-compact domain does not suffice
issues.why_classification: The statements need a genuinely stronger hypothesis and lose their claimed content as an extension to Sobolev topologies, but a correct comparable version (and the intended a-example application, whose F is L^∞-continuous) survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a function $\x \in L^2(\Omega_\X)$, which is extended by zero outside of $\Omega_\X \subseteq \R^m$

issues.failure_explanation: Definition def:mollifier extends x by zero outside Ω_X, so the extension is not in H^k(R^m) unless x and its derivatives vanish on ∂Ω_X. For x≡1 on (0,1) (in H^k for all k) one has x_ξ(0)=1/2 and ||x_ξ-x||_{L^2(0,1)}^2≈cξ, i.e. an O(ξ^{1/2}) error irrespective of k, contradicting the claimed O(ξ^k). This is exactly the situation of the c-example, where x†≥ν>0 cannot vanish on the boundary, so the asserted ||x†_ξ-x†||_{L^2}=O(ξ^2) is false. In addition, even for x∈H^k(R^m) the standard (symmetric, non-moment-vanishing) mollifier only yields order ξ^{min(k-s,2)}, so the claim also fails for k-s≥3. The zero extension further makes x_ξ<ν near ∂Ω_X, so x_ξ need not lie in D(F)={x≥ν}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define x_ξ via mollification of a Sobolev extension (e.g. Stein/reflection extension) of x rather than the zero extension, restrict (v) to k-s≤2 (or to mollifiers with vanishing moments), and verify x_ξ∈D(F).
issues.overall_effect: The c-example's mollification error O(ξ^2) and the resulting rate \autoref{eq:xi} (with term ξ) are unsupported; with the paper's mechanism the boundary error O(ξ^{1/2}) would only give O(ξ^{1/4}). Well-definedness of F[x_ξ] on D(F) is also in question.
issues.title: Lemma le:molli (v) is false for the zero-extension mollifier on bounded domains (and for k-s>2)
issues.why_classification: Requires changing the mollification construction and restricting the lemma, after which the O(ξ^2) claim for the c-example can be recovered; no global architecture changes, but more than a local edit.

issues.failure_explanation: Step 1 of the proof asserts that Fréchet differentiability yields a ξ with ||F[x]-F[x_ξ]||<ε/2 uniformly on an L^2-ball B_r(x*). Fréchet differentiability gives at most local Lipschitz continuity, ||F[x]-F[x_ξ]||≤c||x-x_ξ||_{L^2}, and sup_{x∈B_r(x*)}||x-x_ξ||_{L^2} does not tend to 0 as ξ→0 (high-frequency perturbations of norm r/2 are essentially annihilated by φ_ξ). The statement itself is false for a fixed neighborhood: take F=Id on L^2(Ω_X) (Fréchet differentiable with Lipschitz derivative). F_n[x_ξ] depends on x only through finitely many values x_ξ(s_l)=<x,φ_ξ(s_l-·)>, hence is constant on x*+Z with Z the infinite-dimensional orthogonal complement of these kernels; for z∈Z, ||z||=r/2, the errors at x* and x*+z sum to at least r/2, so ρ_{nξ}≥r/4. If instead r is allowed to shrink with ε the theorem becomes vacuous and useless for the regularization theory, which needs ρ_{nξ}→0 on a fixed neighborhood of x†. The same non-uniformity invalidates the remark's uniform bound O(ρ_{nξ}+ξ^2) and hence the rate \autoref{eq:xi} for the c-example.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must add a compactness-type hypothesis on F (e.g. weak-to-norm sequential continuity on bounded sets, which holds for typical compact forward operators such as the c-example) and replace Step 1 by an argument based on weak compactness of L^2-balls and uniform weak convergence x_ξ⇀x, accepting that no quantitative rate in ξ uniform over the neighborhood is then available.
issues.overall_effect: The L^2 approximation theorem underlying Section 6 is unproven and false in its stated generality; the c-example rate \autoref{eq:xi} and the parameter choice ρ_{nξ}~δ have no support; the paper's claimed extension of neural-operator regularization to Lebesgue spaces is not established.
issues.title: Theorem th:l2 operator apx: mollification error is not uniform on an L^2-ball; the theorem fails for general Fréchet-differentiable F
issues.why_classification: The stated result is refuted by a counterexample within its hypotheses, the proof's key step is invalid, and the only viable resolution changes the hypothesis class and proof mechanism and loses the quantitative ξ-rate advertised in the c-example.
